findings.title: Real-mode runtime wiring unasserted: flipping the handler's watermark flag to True DEMO-stamps every real landlord report with a green suite
findings.evidence: case audit_report.generate(report_data, priv_dir, watermark: False) { — the only test touching handle_get_pdf (pdf_download_writes_audit_log_test, integration/ai_integration_test.gleam:1207+) asserts resp.status == 200 and audit_count == 1, never the PDF body. The golden byte-identity test calls audit_report.generate directly, bypassing the handler.
findings.detail: Spec hard rule 3 (real-mode PDFs byte-identical, no watermark path executes) is pinned at the seam but not at the runtime enforcement point. A one-token flip of the labelled arg watermarks all real reports; no existing unit or integration test would fail.
findings.recommended_fix: In pdf_download_writes_audit_log_test, compare the handler's response body (normalize_metadata) against a fresh audit_report.generate(report_data, priv_dir, watermark: False) render for the same analysis — ~10 lines.

findings.title: Cover page renders TWO stacked watermark layers (~44% combined alpha vs 25% on interiors); the template comment's mechanism is factually wrong
findings.evidence: Cover #set page carries background: demo-watermark AND the cover block ends with an explicit #demo-watermark. Mechanically verified by Perkins: single-page (cover-only) renders with each layer removed differ in bytes AND in rendered pixels (sips PNG diff) — BOTH layers render visibly on the cover. The comment claims the navy block paints over the background; the block has no fill (transparent), so the background watermark is not hidden.
findings.detail: The cover shows two identical overlapping DEMO stamps (25% alpha each → ≈43.75% combined) while interior pages show one (25%) — an unintended inconsistency, and the comment documents a false mechanism. No spec violation: watermark is present, diagonal, readable-through on every page.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop one cover mechanism (delete the explicit trailing #demo-watermark — the page background already delivers it), correct the comment, re-bake the 8 demo PDFs, re-verify. Flag for the k3 visual re-check: cover vs interior watermark consistency.

findings.title: Committed demo PDFs and pdf_prebake.main's watermark: True are unpinned — a stale or regressed re-bake ships unwatermarked demo PDFs with a green suite
findings.evidence: grep of server/test for 'static/demo|report-a-' returns only a comment hit — no test reads server/priv/static/demo/report-*.pdf; the tests re-render via audit_report.generate instead of exercising main() or the served artifacts.
findings.detail: The mechanism is pinned but the served bytes are not. Perkins mechanically re-baked all 8 (RT_DEMO_PRIV_DIR throwaway) and confirmed normalized byte-equality with the committed files at this sha — correct today, unguarded tomorrow.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test that reads 1–2 committed priv/static/demo/report-*.pdf and asserts normalized equality with a fresh generate(watermark: True) render of the same payload.

findings.title: Per-page watermark presence (rule 3) is guaranteed by template construction, not asserted — whole-document inequality can't catch a page-level drop
findings.evidence: Both presence tests assert only normalize_metadata(marked) != normalize_metadata(plain) on whole-document bytes. Interior pages get the watermark only via set page(background:); a regression dropping it from one page style still passes. Four lenses independently flagged this.
findings.detail: Rule 3 demands DEMO on EVERY page; the tests prove presence somewhere. Mechanically confirmed by Perkins: dropping the cover's explicit place keeps both tests green (interior background alone still differentiates).
findings.recommended_fix: Assert per-page presence in one test: count watermark draw ops (e.g. the 40° rotation matrix or 25%-alpha ExtGState references) per page against the page count.

findings.title: skip_if_no_typst / typst_available / priv_dir / normalize_metadata external duplicated across two test files — shared module already exists

findings.title: Test-only normalize_metadata/1 exported from the production FFI module

findings.title: Golden byte-identity pin is deterministic only per typst version; a CI typst bump fails the pin
findings.evidence: The FFI comment itself: 'Everything else is deterministic for a given typst version, template and payload.' PR body documents a deliberate re-bless policy for legitimate template changes.
findings.detail: A typst upgrade changes version-stamped output bytes and fails pdf_real_mode_render_matches_golden_test with no normalization for version fields. Known, documented trade — bites only on toolchain bumps.
findings.recommended_fix: Acceptable as-is. If it bites: pin the CI typst version or extend normalize_metadata to strip version-stamped metadata.

findings.title: AC 'two distinct PDF paths' delivered as two payloads through the single demo path — documented deviation, intent satisfied
findings.evidence: demo_reports_carry_watermark_on_two_distinct_paths_test renders a-aoife (multi-page showcase) and a-liam (short) — both via pdf_prebake.to_report_data → audit_report.generate.
findings.detail: The producer survey (PR body) proves the demo has exactly one PDF path; two distinct report shapes is the strongest available interpretation of the AC. Accepted.
findings.recommended_fix: Optionally rename to demo_reports_carry_watermark_on_two_distinct_reports_test to avoid overstating path coverage.

findings.title: watermark --input pair appended after the positional output path
findings.evidence: typst_args = list.append([..., template_path, output_path], watermark_args) — the flag pair lands after both positionals. Works today (all bakes/tests used it; clap accepts interspersed options).
findings.detail: Relies on typst's parser accepting options after positionals. If typst ever tightens parsing, the demo pre-bake breaks at runtime only.
findings.recommended_fix: Build the argv with the --input pair before template_path so options precede positionals.

findings.title: No-op 'let _ = application_id' in payload_for error branch
findings.evidence: Error(_) -> { let _ = application_id panic as "demo payload missing" } — the parameter is already used in the list.find closure above; the discard suppresses nothing.
findings.detail: Pure dead line, contrary to the no-dead-code rule.
